beats.text: Same move, same truck. Thirty-four kilometres closer to work: zero deduction. Forty-three closer: the whole move counts.
Riley took a new job in twenty twenty-five. The old home was fifty-two kilometres from it.
The rule: your new home must be at least forty kilometres closer to the new work, by the shortest public route.
An apartment eighteen kilometres away is only thirty-four closer. Nothing to claim.
One nine kilometres away is forty-three closer. Now the forty-two hundred dollar move counts: truck, travel, up to fifteen days of temporary living.
The twist: it only comes off income earned at the new job. Riley started in December and earned twenty-five hundred. The other seventeen hundred carries forward.
So measure the route before you sign the lease, and keep every receipt.
Next: first-time home buyers, and what changed. Follow so you don't miss it.
